correctness.rationale: The scale ratios have log increment \(\log(q_x/p_x)=-2\mu_x+O(\mu_x^3)\), giving \(\rho_x\sim Kx^{-2\beta-1}(\log x)^{-2d}\) and a summable scale tail. The exact hitting-probability formula gives \(h(x)\); its adjacent ratio yields transformed drift \(\mu_x^h=(1/2-\beta)/x-d/(x\log x)+O(1/(x(\log x)^2))\). Alexander's Theorem 2.1 applies with \(\delta=2\beta-1>-1\) and slowly varying factor \(L(x)\sim K'(\log x)^{-2d}\), so the conditional first-return mass is regularly varying with index \(-\beta-1\). The local defective-renewal asymptotic then yields \(P_0(X_{2n}=0)\sim Cn^{-\beta-1}(\log n)^{-2d}\), \(C>0\). The conditional \(\beta\)-moment test reduces to \(\sum_{n\ge2}1/[n(\log n)^{2d}]\), which converges exactly when \(d>1/2\). All statements are asymptotic and no finite experiment substitutes for proof.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a sharp local-return law and the exact logarithmic boundary between finite and infinite conditional return-time moments at a critical Lamperti drift. The coefficient \(d\) is a natural second-order invariant: the power exponent alone does not decide the boundary. The result supplies a concrete transient-chain local-limit example for a gap explicitly noted in the 2022 source, rather than a numerical experiment or an arbitrary parameter slice.
